business_model: Freemium or free-trial customer acquisition followed by recurring individual subscriptions, artist subscriptions, API subscriptions, custom enterprise contracts, and custom licensing or white-label engagements. Enterprise pricing varies by team size, accounts, and business needs and carries a stated one-year minimum commitment.
pricing_model: Consumer plans are shown with monthly and discounted annual-billing equivalents: Creator $16.99/month or $11.04/month with annual billing; Artist Starter $29.99 or $19.49; Artist Pro $35.99 or $23.39; Artist Unlimited $50 or $32.50. API Starter is $29.99/month for up to 100 songs per month and is limited to new signups and organizations with up to three employees. API Pro is $300/month for up to 1,000 songs per month with a six-month minimum commitment. Custom API plans are available. Enterprise uses custom pricing and flexible terms, with a one-year minimum commitment. The website also states that API pricing may be based on generations, minutes, or volume tiers, creating some ambiguity relative to the published song-count plans.

business_risks: Very strong absolute copyright promises could create reputational or legal exposure if users receive claims, disputes, or platform enforcement

marketing_message: SOUNDRAW positions itself as the safest and most ethical AI beat maker: a fast, customizable, studio-ready music generator trained only on rights-controlled in-house recordings, allowing creators, artists, developers, and businesses to make, edit, monetize, and embed royalty-free music without copyright concerns.
messaging_gaps: The website does not consistently explain the boundary between ownership, licensing, royalty-free use, and restrictions after subscription cancellation
Absolute statements such as 'legally yours,' 'copyright-free,' 'no strikes ever,' and '100% safe' are not accompanied by caveats, enforcement procedures, or legal guarantees in the supplied evidence
The '#1 ethical AI music generator' and 'trusted by millions' claims lack methodology or direct-user definitions
It is unclear which capabilities are universally available versus restricted by plan, especially stems, WAV downloads, tempo and key editing, looping, and video preview
The distinction among Store BGM, Space Music, BGM for Physical Spaces, and custom ambient-music systems is not clearly articulated
SOUNDRAW Grid's purpose, pricing, availability, and relationship to the web product are missing
The practical meaning of 'infinite' or 'unlimited' generation and downloads is not reconciled with fair-use rules or API quotas
The website offers both fixed API song-count plans and a statement that pricing may depend on generations, minutes, or volume, without clarifying when each applies
